core_obligations: Assume each base change f_i is a quasi-compact immersion and deduce that f is quasi-compact and separated (proof lines 6269-6279).
Form the scheme-theoretic image factorization X -> Z -> Y and identify the ideal cutting out Z (proof lines 6280-6285).
Use flat base change, with f separated, to identify f_{i,*} O_{X_i} with the pullback of f_* O_X (proof lines 6286-6290).
Deduce that Y_i x_Y Z is cut out by the pullback ideal, so each X_i -> Y_i x_Y Z is an open immersion (proof lines 6291-6296).
Descend the openness to get that X -> Z is an open immersion and conclude (proof lines 6296-6300).
proof_roadmap: Quasi-compactness and separatedness of f (proof lines 6269-6279).
The scheme-theoretic image and its ideal (proof lines 6280-6285).
Base change of the ideal via flat base change (proof lines 6286-6293).
Descent of the open immersion and conclusion (proof lines 6294-6300).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts that the property 'f is a quasi-compact immersion' is fpqc local on the base (statement lines 6262-6266). The proof fixes an fpqc covering, writes the base changes f_i, and assumes each is a quasi-compact immersion; these are separated, so descent of quasi-compactness and separatedness makes f quasi-compact and separated; the scheme-theoretic image factorization X -> Z -> Y is then formed, the closed subscheme Z being cut out by Ker(O_Y -> f_* O_X) because f is quasi-compact; flat base change (using separatedness of f) identifies f_{i,*} O_{X_i} with the pullback of f_* O_X, so Y_i x_Y Z is cut out by the pullback of the ideal, whence each X_i -> Y_i x_Y Z is an open immersion by the characterisation of quasi-compact immersions; descent of open immersions then makes X -> Z an open immersion, so f is an immersion, quasi-compactness having already been established (proof lines 6268-6300). The level is H3: the ideal-theoretic description of the scheme-theoretic image and its base change is the load-bearing computation, and it is carried out explicitly.
